quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible, use turn signals, keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: A good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Encourage the tailgater to pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage the tailgater to pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: If it is safe, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Continue the passing maneuver if you see an upcoming bridge.
Continue the passing maneuver if you see an upcoming railroad crossing.
Try to pass more than one vehicle at a time to save time.
Not follow another vehicle that is passing a car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not follow another vehicle that is passing a car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Do not pass if oncoming vehicles or pedestrians are near, or if bridges, curves, hills, intersections, or railroad crossings are ahead. Do not pass more than one vehicle at a time. Do not follow a vehicle that is already passing.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time, you should:

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is best.
Just start riding. Most bikes are the same.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Before riding a new bike, check its safety and maintenance, find where everything is, and practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how it works.

questions.question: If you have only one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding ability. Any amount of alcohol is not safe when riding.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: You can reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers can keep you awake, but they cannot lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing so other drivers can see you. Reflective materials help even more.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the maximum speed limit.
Ride at a speed where you can stop within your headlight's light.
Ride as fast as everyone else.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride at a speed where you can stop within your headlight's light.
questions.explanation: At night, ride at a speed that lets you stop within the area lit by your headlight. Slow down when you cannot see well.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking quickly makes alcohol build up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your system.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the left third of the lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can prevent the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see to the sides as needed for safe riding.
Can be dangerous for the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You can see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What should you think about first when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection.
questions.explanation: Protection is most important when buying a helmet. Choose one that fits well, fastens securely, and is DOT-approved.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what matters most?
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection.
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important factor when buying a helmet.

questions.question: To avoid collisions, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep enough space around the motorcycle.
Ride down the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space around the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle to avoid collisions. Maintain this space when following other vehicles, being followed, passing, or being passed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, you should make sure it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or torn straps.

questions.question: In a crash, a rider wearing a helmet is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than a person without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as a person without a helmet.
More likely to survive than a person without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than a person without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets during a crash.

questions.question: When a tailgater is following you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
Do not make motorcycle riders safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: Avoid riding next to another vehicle because:

options.text: The driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot and they won't see you. Also, the vehicle may block your path to escape if danger appears.
